shell.demoHint: Not connected to hpk serve: this is sample data. Run hpk serve to see your projects.
shell.noProjectBody: hpk serve is running, but no project has been added. Add one from a terminal; hpk asks before it reads anything.
shell.demoPageBody: hpk serve does not feed this page yet, so what you see here is example data, not your setup. Use the hpk command line for it for now.
shell.noProjectSetup: Set up hpk and add a project

mode.title: Working mode

manual.name: Manual
manual.desc: The agent reads and drafts on its own. Every write and every command waits for you.

ask.name: Ask
ask.desc: The agent works inside its worktree and commits locally. It stops at each decision point and at every red line.

auto.name: Auto
auto.desc: A small model decides routine approvals for you and logs each one so you can undo it. Red lines still stop and wait for a human.

mode.redLinesBody: Push, delete, secrets, agent-control files, model changes, core wiki pages, sharing knowledge and sending data out always wait for a human — in every mode.
mode.seeGates: See all decision points and red lines

track.aria: Track diagram of lanes and the sessions working in them

legend.danger: Held: red line or duplicate work
legend.route: Blue = route of the session you point at

overview.title: {project}
overview.lede: Every lane, who holds which block of work, and what is waiting for you.
overview.keysHint: Click the list, then: j / k to move, a approves a red line, d denies, Enter opens. Elsewhere, g then a opens Approvals.

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.lede: Every main chat and the sub-tasks it split off. Sub-tasks work in their own worktree and report back to their main chat.
sessions.viaHpk: HPK Console (ACP) — you can chat here
sessions.readOnlyNote: This session was started outside HPK. You can see its status and ask how it is going, but not chat with it here.
sessions.askSent: Asked {num} for status. The answer will arrive without interrupting it.

form.title: Task name
form.titleHint: The title follows the project template automatically.
form.briefPh: What to do, what done looks like, which wiki pages to read first.
form.briefHint: The brief also lists this project's red lines and the summary format to send back.
form.claimNote: Before it starts, hpk checks the board. If someone already holds this work, you will be asked what to do.
form.started: Started “{title}”. It will appear on the board once it claims its paths.

hint.keys: Enter sends · Shift+Enter new line · / commands · # wiki pages · Ctrl+K new chat · Alt+↑↓ switch chat

chat.readOnlyHint: You can only ask this session for its status.
chat.permitTitle: The agent stopped at a red line
chat.accountTitle: AI account this session is using
chat.newOptions: More ways to start a chat
chat.deleteBody: Delete “{title}” and its conversation? The session’s wiki notes and commits are kept. This cannot be undone.
chat.renameHint: The title keeps the project template unless you change it here.
chat.savedToWiki: Saved as a wiki draft — waits for your approval
chat.editNote: Messages after this one are replaced. Fork first to keep them.

summary.title: Sub-task finished
summary.question: Question
summary.notVerified: Not verified yet. Merging needs a passing test, review or verify.
summary.askTestsText: Run the tests for this change and report the results.

chat.compressed: Context compressed: {from} → {to} tokens. The full conversation is kept.
chat.emptyLog: No messages yet. Say what you want done.
chat.btwAnswer: Side answer to “{q}” — not added to the conversation or the wiki.

model.heading: Model for this chat
model.changeBody: Switching from {from} to {to} drops the prompt cache and may change behaviour. This is a red line, so it needs your confirmation.
model.redLineNote: Changing model mid-chat is a red line

ctx.explain: Context is how much of the conversation the model holds at once. Compressing summarises older turns; the full history stays saved.

newc.lede: Describe the goal. The agent plans it and splits it into sub-tasks by itself — you follow everything from this one chat.

coordinator.d: A top-level chat that plans and opens children.

child.d: Works in its own worktree and reports back to its parent.

newc.name: Name
newc.firstPh: e.g. Add CSV and PDF export to invoices, with tests. Stop before pushing.

plan.label: Plan the next version
plan.text: Plan the next version. Read BOARD.md and the wiki first, then propose lanes and open a child per lane.

review.label: Review open lanes
review.text: Review every open lane: check git in each worktree, not the board prose, and give me a table of real status.

yesterday.label: What happened yesterday
yesterday.text: Summarise what happened in this project since yesterday from the wiki log and session summaries.

tests.label: Fix failing tests
tests.text: Run the test suite, find the failing tests and fix them inside a worktree. Stop before pushing.

newc.claimNote: hpk checks the board first, so the same work is never started twice.
newc.inherited: Inherited — change for this chat only
newc.worktree: Work in a new git worktree
newc.settingsNote: Changing the model later in the chat is a red line and will ask you first.
newc.splitNote: Enter to start · Shift+Enter new line
newc.nameAuto: Leave empty to use the first line of your message

chat.settingsAria: Model, reasoning effort and mode for this chat

delivery.pendingHint: Held until the agent finishes its current step
delivery.readHint: The agent read this and applied it
delivery.unusedHint: The step stopped before the agent read this. It was not applied.

permit.keys: Keys on this card: 1 deny · 2 allow once · 3 allow for session

recall.title: Wiki recalled into this chat
recall.droppedTitle: Left out: did not fit the budget
recall.budget: Budget per turn: {budget} tokens. Anything left out is named here.

chat.shareBody: Everyone sees this chat on the board. The people you tick can also read its messages. Owners of the Console can read every chat.
chat.shareNobody: Nobody else is in the team yet.

switch.title: Switch model
switch.lede: The chat keeps its memory: the brief ({brief}) and recalled wiki pages ({recall}) always go along. The ring shows how full the history would be on each model.
switch.rule: Auto: up to 60% full, the whole history goes along; above that it is compacted to a summary plus the last 20 messages, and the full history stays searchable. Another provider is a red line.
switch.policy: This project allows local models only, so remote models are locked.
switch.busy: The agent is answering. Switch when the turn ends.
switch.notLive: Open this chat in hpk serve to switch models.
switch.unavailable: {m} is not offered for this chat any more
switch.costHint: Input cost of the first message on this model. Nothing is cached there yet, so every token is billed in full.
switch.ringHint: Full history: {full}% of the {win} window. Sent: {sent}%.
switch.crossBody: Moving this chat to {m} sends its history to {p}, another provider. The prompt cache starts over and thinking from the old model is dropped.

way.continueHint: Fits: the whole conversation goes along. Thinking blocks the new model cannot read are dropped.
way.compactHint: Too full: Hermes summarises older turns and keeps the last 20 messages. The full history stays searchable.

done.continue: Now on {m}, with the whole history
done.compact: Now on {m}: history compacted, the last 20 messages kept

ask.label: Question for {m}
ask.placeholder: What should the other model look at?
ask.note: A sub-task answers and reports back here. This chat keeps its model and cache.
ask.started: {m} is on it. The answer comes back here as a summary.
ask.crossTitle: Ask a model from another provider?
ask.crossBody: Asking {m} sends the question and this chat's brief to {p}, another provider. This chat stays on its own model.

approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.lede: Everything waiting for a human, oldest risk first. Decide with the keyboard: j / k to move, a to approve, d to deny.
approvals.undoNote: Undo requested. The session will be asked to revert if it already acted.
approvals.emptyDetail: When an agent stops at a red line or asks a question, it shows up here.
approvals.redLineNote: Red lines wait for a human in every mode. Your decision is written to the audit log.

push.long: Push, tag, open a merge request, or merge into the main branch.

delete.long: Delete files, folders, worktrees, branches, databases or wiki pages.

secrets.long: Read or print .env files and other secrets.

control.long: Edit AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, SOUL.md, skills, project.yaml or the wiki SCHEMA.

model.long: Switch a chat to another provider's model, or spend beyond the budget.

wikicore.long: Change decisions/, architecture/ or people/ in the wiki.

promote.long: Promote knowledge to the shared wiki or change a project's privacy mode.

egress.long: Send anything outside this machine except the configured channel.

wiki.title: Wiki
wiki.lede: {pages} pages of project knowledge. Every claim has a source. Rules live in the repo, not here.
wiki.historyNote: History comes from the wiki's own git log.
wiki.noDrafts: No drafts waiting. New knowledge from sessions will appear here.
wiki.batchHint: Type approve or discard followed by numbers, then press Enter.
wiki.changesAsked: Sent back to the session with your note

approvedToast.one: 1 page saved to the wiki and committed
approvedToast.other: {n} pages saved to the wiki and committed

wiki.logSub: Append-only. Every write, by anyone, in time order.
wiki.empty: No approved pages yet. Pages appear here after a person approves a draft.
wiki.emptyDrafts: {n} drafts are waiting in the Drafts tab.
wiki.promoteBody: hpk makes a redacted copy (no project names, paths, URLs or people) as a draft in the shared wiki you pick. Nothing is shared until a person approves it there; you can edit the copy first on the Privacy page.
wiki.promoted: Draft {n} is waiting on the Privacy page.

promoteToSub.team: every project can learn from it; an owner approves
promoteToSub.mine: only for you, across your projects; you approve

board.title: Board
board.lede: Who is working on what. hpk keeps claims in board.db and writes {file} for people to read.
board.diagramSub: One box per claim. An overlap is marked on the boxes it touches.
board.alertsSub: Checked at start, on every commit and nightly · 0 tokens
board.whoBody: Type a path or task. The answer comes from the board, without disturbing any session.
board.dupBody: Session {a} wants to change files that {b} ({owner}) is already working on. Last heartbeat {ago}.
board.dupAutoNote: In Auto mode the agent may choose to wait or work elsewhere on its own. Working together or taking over always needs a person.

wait.d: Hold this part until the other claim is released. You will be told when it is.
wait.done: Waiting. You will be notified when the claim is released.

other.d: Pick a free block from the board instead.
other.done: Moved to a free block on the board.

together.d: Send a message to the other session to split the work.
together.done: Message sent to the other session (queued, not interrupting).

takeover.d: Ask the claim's owner, or an owner or maintainer, to hand the work over.
takeover.done: Takeover request sent to the claim owner.

gates.title: Modes & red lines
gates.lede: How often the agent must ask you, which points always come to a human, and the record of every decision.
gates.modeSub: Override per session or lane from the top bar

start.d: Missing facts are asked for in one question.

plan.d: The plan is posted before work begins.
plan.auto: Goes ahead if in agreed scope

lanes.d: Child sessions in their own worktrees.

childStuck.d: Real questions always reach a person.

wiki.d: lessons / versions / glossary vs core pages.

weekly.d: Read the week's summary; undo what Auto did.

gates.rlTitle: Red lines stop the agent in every mode
gates.rlBody: Built-in lines cannot be removed. Add your project's own lines below — they are stored in project.yaml.
gates.rlPh: e.g. Never edit an applied migration

audit.title: Audit log
audit.files: Stored in the project folder (decisions.jsonl and audit.log). Nothing here can be edited.

digest.title: Today Auto decided {n} things for you
digest.sub: Sent at 18:00 on days Auto ran
digest.how: Wiki changes revert with git; file changes use Hermes checkpoints.

jobs.title: Scheduled jobs
jobs.lede: Background work that keeps knowledge growing. Each job has a token budget and stops to ask before going over it.

desc.nightly: Today's sessions and git log → raw notes and drafts
desc.weekly: Contradictions, stale pages, pages nothing links to
desc.digest: Summary of Auto's decisions, only on days it ran

rule.lock: One run at a time per project (lock).
rule.resume: A failed run continues where it stopped next time.
rule.budget: Over budget → stop and ask, never silently continue.
rule.zero: Checks that need no thinking run as scripts and cost 0 tokens.
rule.batch: Night jobs use batch models where the provider offers them.

projects.title: Projects
projects.lede: Personal projects are only yours; team projects have members and roles. Every project uses a Profile, which uses a Process.
projects.oneProfile: Switching project switches the Hermes profile. Nothing from one project is visible inside another unless that project is Shared and you approved the knowledge.

sectionSub.team: Shared with members · approvals by role
sectionSub.personal: Only you · your own accounts and wiki

projects.chainNote: A Profile can be used by several projects. Switching project switches its Profile in Hermes; the wiki, board and privacy stay with the project.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lede: How knowledge from {project} may leave it.

shared.name: Shared
shared.desc: Can add to the shared wiki, but only after you approve a cleaned-up copy.

private.name: Private
private.desc: Never writes to the shared wiki. Still learns from general lessons there.

isolated.name: Isolated
isolated.desc: Nothing goes in or out. For highly confidential work.

privacy.changeNote: Changing from Private or Isolated to Shared needs approval, and old knowledge is never promoted automatically.
privacy.needsApproval: Making this project Shared needs an owner's approval. Request sent.
privacy.promoLede: General lessons found by the weekly lint. Names, paths and people are removed before anything leaves the project.
privacy.editRedaction: Opened the cleaned copy for editing
privacy.promoted: Shared to the wiki of all your projects
privacy.promoOff: This project is {mode}. Nothing from it is ever offered for sharing.

team.title: Team
team.lede: People who use this server, what they can approve, and their budgets.
team.authBody: Team mode needs sign-in. HPK Console supports OIDC (Keycloak, Authentik, Google…), passkeys, or a trusted header from your reverse proxy.
team.removeAsk: Removing {name} needs confirmation from another owner
team.inviteNote: The invite works only after sign-in is set up. People see only the projects their group maps to.
team.personalBody: Only you can see and approve work here. To work with others, create a team project or change this one to a team project in its settings.
team.signInBody: This Console is shared by a team. Use the personal token an owner gave you (hpk team add). It stays signed in for 12 hours.
team.signInProxy: This Console signs you in through your organisation's sign-in page. Open it through that address.
team.tokenOnce: Token for {id}. It is shown only now.
team.tokenOnceHint: Give it to them privately. hpk keeps only its hash; if it is lost, issue a new one.
team.rotateConfirm: Issue a new token for {id}? Their old token stops working.
team.removeConfirm: Remove {id} from the team? They are signed out at once.
team.inviteSub: They sign in with the token shown after you add them.
team.name: Name (optional)
team.ledeLive: Who can use this Console and what each person may decide. Sign-in: {auth}.
team.rolesNote: Owner: settings, privacy, people. Maintainer: red lines, modes, core wiki pages. Member: chats and general wiki drafts. Viewer: reads only. A chat belongs to whoever started it.
team.capsHint: What the chats this person starts may cost, across projects. At a cap, their chats get no more tools and they cannot start new ones until it is raised or the period ends. Project caps still apply.

settings.title: Settings
settings.lede: Connection to Hermes, notifications, budgets and appearance.
settings.languageHint: All text comes from i18n/<language>.json — edit those files to change any wording.
settings.licenseValue: MIT + Commons Clause (source-available, not for sale)
settings.dataValue: Stays in your Hermes home folder
settings.sampleValue: Sample data — not a real project
settings.channelHint: Private and isolated projects always use the console only.
settings.batch: Group notifications (at most one every 5 minutes, except red lines)
settings.ingestHint: Analysis stops and asks before going over this.
settings.motionHint: Track draw-in, flowing light, route lighting and transitions. Your system’s reduce-motion setting always wins.

ap.title: Appearance
ap.sub: Saved in this browser only. Each person on the team can pick their own.

hermes.fix: Install or add hermes to PATH

acp.d: Used to start, chat with and approve sessions

auth.d: Required before binding beyond this machine

hookLatency.d: Target under 30 ms (80 ms on Windows)

notif.title: Notifications
notif.batching: Grouped every 5 minutes. Red lines and duplicate work arrive at once.

wizard.title: Add project
wizard.lede: hpk asks before it reads anything, shows the cost first, and never opens secrets.

consent.title: Analyse this project and add its knowledge to the wiki?
consent.pathHint: A git repository on this machine.
consent.note: Nothing is read until you continue. .env files, secrets and anything in .gitignore are never opened.

full.d: Docs, notes, ADRs, agent files, CI and config.

skip.d: Create an empty wiki. Knowledge builds up from sessions.

privacy.title: How private is this project?
privacy.local: Use only local models for analysis (Ollama / LM Studio)
privacy.change: You can change this later in Privacy.

scan.title: Scan
scan.zeroBody: The scan is a script: file tree, languages, git history. No AI involved.

estimate.title: What will be read, and what it costs
estimate.lede: Untick anything you do not want read. The estimate updates as you go.
estimate.models: Reading uses the cheap model; one pass of the main model writes the drafts.
estimate.over: This is over the project's analysis limit (400k tokens). It will stop and ask before going over.

ingest.title: Reading
ingest.lede: Facts are written to raw/ with their source. Nothing becomes a wiki page without your approval.
ingest.paused: Paused. You can resume from where it stopped.

drafts.title: {n} pages drafted
drafts.lede: Untick any you do not want. Core pages are marked.
drafts.later: You can also review them later in Wiki → Drafts.

health.title: Knowledge health
health.lede: Problems found in the project's own documents. Tick the ones to fix.
health.repoNote: Fixes to files in the repository are proposed separately and need your approval.

config.title: Project settings
config.lede: Detected from the repository. Check before saving.
config.where: Saved to the {name} profile as hpk/project.yaml. The wiki starts with the approved pages.
config.inherits: everything else is inherited from the profile and its process

setup.title: Personal or team, and which profile?

kindDesc.team: Members, roles and approvals by role. Board and claims are shared.
kindDesc.personal: Only you. Your own accounts, private by default.

setup.membersHint: Roles are set on the Team page. You can add people later.
setup.profileHint: The profile brings its process. You can override single settings for this project later.

accounts.title: AI accounts
accounts.lede: Add as many accounts per provider as you like, put them in order, and hpk switches to the next one when an account runs out.
accounts.safeBody: Accounts are saved in Hermes' credential store. This page only shows a masked fingerprint, never the key, and never sends it anywhere except to the provider.
accounts.noneUsable: No usable account — work is held
accounts.rowAria: {n}. {label}, {status}. Alt and arrow keys move it.
accounts.switchWhen: Switch to the next account when

quota.d: rate limit or usage limit reached (429)

budget.d: the cap you set on this account

accounts.returnTo: Go back to the first account

ret.on_reset: As soon as its limit resets
ret.next_session: At the start of the next session
ret.never: Never — stay on the account that works

sticky.t: Keep running sessions on their account
sticky.d: switching mid-session loses the prompt cache, so it only happens when the account fails

cross.d: off by default: a different provider means a different model, which needs a human

accounts.crossOn: Cross-provider fallback on — it will still ask before changing model
accounts.notify: Tell me every time an account is switched
accounts.accessTitle: Which projects may use which account
accounts.accessSub: For example: company work only on the company account

form.label: Name
form.labelHint: You can add several accounts to the same provider.
form.keyHint: Sent straight to Hermes' credential store. It is never shown again.
form.oauthNote: You will sign in with the provider in a new window. hpk never sees your password.
form.hermesNote: Pick an account Hermes already knows (hermes auth list).
form.orderNote: New accounts go to the end of the order. Drag to change it.

accounts.added: {label} added at the end of the order
accounts.noneLeft: No usable account left. Work on this provider is held until one resets.

cat.title: Work categories
cat.sub: Each sub-task gets a category. The category picks its model and what to fall back to.
cat.order: Order of fallback: first the next account for the same model (above), then the next model in the chain. Changing model is still a red line for a running sub-task.
cat.note: Saved in hpk’s own settings. Hermes’ config is never rewritten. Changes apply to new sub-tasks.
cat.saved: Saved. New sub-tasks use this chain.

desc.review: checks, reviews and the verify step

setup.title: Set up hpk on this computer
setup.lede: hpk works with Hermes Agent. Two things first; nothing is downloaded or changed until you agree.

explain.process: How work flows: mode, decision points, red lines, board, scheduled jobs. Reusable.
explain.profile: Who the agent is: models, AI accounts, skills, personality. Built on one Process.
explain.project: What it works on: repository, wiki, privacy, people. Personal or team. Uses one Profile.
explain.rule: Project overrides Profile, Profile overrides Process. Red lines only add up — a lower layer can add one, never remove one.

setup.unusedProcess: No profile uses this process yet.
setup.processNote: Changing a process changes every profile and project built on it, except settings they override.
setup.profileNote: One profile can serve many projects — personal and team. Each project keeps its own wiki, board and privacy.
setup.effNote: Struck-through values are overridden by a lower layer. Overrides are saved in the project’s project.yaml.
setup.hermesWhy: hpk needs Hermes Agent for chats, hooks and scheduled jobs. hpk looks for hermes on PATH.
setup.offerTitle: hpk can install the tested Hermes Agent {version} for you
setup.offerBody: Into hpk's own folder ({dir}), with its own portable Python. It does not change a system Python or anything else on this computer.
setup.total: Total: about {dl} MB to download, {disk} MB on disk (estimates).
setup.agree: I agree to download and install these from the sources shown
setup.self: Or install it yourself (docs/install.md) and reload this page.
setup.unsupported: There is no tested installer for this platform ({platform}). Install Hermes Agent yourself (docs/install.md).
setup.failed: The install stopped. Nothing outside hpk's folder was changed; you can try again.
setup.hpkWait: Next, hpk is added to Hermes (after Hermes is installed).
setup.hpkWhat: Same as hpk install --yes: skills and hooks in {config}, with a backup.
setup.hpkNote: Hermes asks you once to allow each new hook the first time it runs. Your projects and wikis are not touched.
setup.modelBody: Hermes needs a model account (Nous Portal, Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter or a local model). Connect one in a terminal:
setup.ready: Ready. Next: add your first project.
setup.notYet: You can continue now and finish this later.

ev.aria: Evidence: stage and how sure we are

plan.title: Plan
plan.graphAria: Plan: sub-tasks and what each one waits on. Choose a sub-task to act on it.
plan.steerLede: It keeps working and applies this to the remaining steps. Ctrl+Enter sends.
plan.steerPh: Tell this sub-task what to change
plan.boardEmpty: No chat has split work yet. Start a chat and the agent draws its plan here.

wikiAdmit.title: Save to wiki?
wikiAdmit.hidden: Hidden: it looks like a secret. It is not shown or stored.
wikiAdmit.target: Becomes a draft at {path}. A draft still needs approval before it joins the wiki.
wikiAdmit.rules: Rules: secrets are always refused. Logs and task progress are refused unless you keep them. Very short notes are deferred.

done.keep: Draft created. It waits for approval.
done.defer: Deferred. It is in the admission log with its reason.
done.refused: Refused and logged. Nothing was saved.

wikiAdmit.logSub: Every save request: kept, refused or deferred, with the reason

reason.keep: Stands on its own and names its source (session {src}).
reason.secret: Looks like a secret (key, password or .env). Secrets never go to the wiki.
reason.log: Looks like a log or test output, not knowledge. Logs stay in the session.
reason.progress: This is progress on the current task, not something to remember later.
reason.short: Too short to stand alone. Say what was decided and why first.

live.rlHow: Your own red lines go into project.yaml (gates.red_lines_extra). A line written as re:<pattern> is enforced on commands; plain text is shown to the agent as a rule.
live.digestEmpty: Auto let nothing through in the last 24 hours.
live.localOnlyNote: Enforced: hpk sees where each request of a session goes. On a local-only project, tools are refused for a session that uses (or once used) a model outside this machine. Hosts in privacy.local_hosts also count as this machine.
live.openUpConfirm: Open {name} up to {mode}? Knowledge already in its wiki is not promoted.
live.jobsNoneTitle: No jobs are scheduled for this project yet
live.jobsNoneBody: Creating them adds jobs to Hermes cron, which runs a model. Review the plan and agree in a terminal:
live.runsEmpty: No runs yet. Runs show here after Hermes cron runs a job.
live.wizardLede: Point hpk at a folder. The scan and checks read names, sizes and links only, and never open secret files. Nothing is read with a model until you start it.
live.noSources: No documents found to read. You can still add the project.
live.priceNote: Estimate at ${price} per million tokens; the real price depends on the model.
live.healthLede: Checks the project's own documents against its files: missing READMEs, broken links, paths that no longer exist. 0 tokens.
live.healthClean: No problems found in the documents.
live.configLede: This is what hpk writes. You can edit project.yaml at any time.
live.configWhere: Written to <hermes home>/hpk/projects/<name>/: project.yaml, its wiki, and the reading queue. Your project folder is not changed.
live.name: Project name
live.addedBody: project.yaml, the wiki and the reading queue are ready. If the folder is a git repository, its history is in the wiki's raw notes.
live.ingestTitle: Reading the documents uses a model
live.ingestBody: It runs one source at a time and stops at the budget. Start it when you are ready:

acc.lede: Hermes' credential pool, read with `hermes auth list`. hpk never sees a key.
acc.label: Account
acc.none: Hermes has no pooled accounts yet.
acc.manageSub: Adding, ordering and removing accounts stays in Hermes, so keys never pass through hpk.
acc.ledeManage: Hermes' credential pool. Changes run hermes auth, so keys stay in Hermes; hpk never stores, logs or shows a key.
acc.removeConfirm: Remove {label} from {provider}? Hermes stops using it at once.
acc.addSub: For providers that sign in with a key. The key goes to Hermes and is not kept by hpk.
acc.keyHint: Sent once over this connection to hermes auth add. Over the network the Console must use HTTPS.
acc.needBoth: Give a provider and a key.
acc.oauthNote: Accounts that sign in through a browser (Claude, Codex, Nous) are added in a terminal: hermes auth add <provider>.
acc.windowsNote: On Windows Hermes reads keys from the keyboard, so add keys in a terminal. You can reorder, reset and remove them here.

live.setupNote: Profiles are your real Hermes profiles. hpk has one process (its defaults) until processes ship. You can change a project's mode, board and language here; the model stays in Hermes because changing it is a red line.
live.channelNote: Reports go to the Console. Other channels are not built yet; private and isolated projects stay local anyway.
live.batchNote: Notices are batched: at most one per kind every 5 minutes, except duplicate-work alerts.
live.nightlyHint: A run that goes over this is stopped at its next tool call, then the job pauses. Cache reads count a tenth.
live.moneyNote: Costs come from the usage Hermes reports for each request, at the models.dev prices Hermes keeps. At a cap, agents get no more tools, the Console starts no sessions and scheduled jobs pause, until a person raises it or the day or month ends.
live.soloBody: Team mode (sign-in, roles, approvers) comes in v0.2. Until then this Console belongs to the person running hpk serve.
live.localOk: Profile {profile} uses {where}, which is on this machine. Console sessions may start.
live.localBad: Profile {profile} sends requests to {where}. Console sessions and scheduled jobs for this project are refused until that profile uses a local model.
live.dailyHint: Every job pauses when the project's jobs together go over this. Cache reads count a tenth, like the price.
live.usdNumber: Use an amount in USD, such as 5 or 2.50.
live.notifyHint: A Hermes send target: telegram, slack:#builds, discord:#ops … Sent with hermes send, so the token stays in Hermes. Empty = Console only. You get: approvals waiting, chats that finished a turn.
live.notifyLocal: This project is private or isolated: notices stay in the Console, on this machine.
live.runNowConfirm: Run the {name} job now? Its script runs first (0 tokens); if there is new work, Hermes runs a model, up to {budget} tokens.
live.editRedactHint: This is the copy that goes to the shared wiki. Remove anything that points back to this project. Text that looks like a secret is refused.

git.title: Git
git.lede: The project history as a picture. Every command shows the exact git it runs; history rewrites get an undo point first; red lines ask a person.
git.sample: Sample data — not connected to a repository yet
git.hint: Click a commit to inspect it, right-click for actions. Drag a branch label onto another to merge, rebase or open a draft PR.
git.dragHint: Click for actions · drag onto another branch to merge, rebase or open a PR
git.undoPointBody: hpk records where every branch pointed (refs/hpk/undo/…), so Undo puts it all back.
git.rewritePushed: This branch is already pushed: the new history replaces it on the remote (git push --force-with-lease, which refuses if someone else pushed meanwhile). A person approves.
git.redLineBody: A person approves before this runs.
git.noUndo: No undo points yet. hpk saves one before every rebase, reset and branch delete.
git.conflictStop: The rebase stopped: both sides changed the same lines
git.conflictBody: {a} and {b} both edited this part. Pick what the file should say, then continue — or abort and nothing changes.
git.orAbort: or give up and go back

tip.fetch: Download new commits; changes nothing of yours
tip.pull: Bring the current branch up to date (fast-forward only)
tip.push: Send your commits to the remote (red line)
tip.branch: Start a branch from the current commit
tip.interactive: Reorder, squash, reword or drop commits on this branch
tip.undo: Go back to an undo point

w.fetch: Downloads new commits and branches from the remote. Nothing you have is changed.
w.pull: Brings {b} up to date with the remote, only if it can move forward without a merge.
w.push: Sends the commits of {b} to the remote.
w.branch: Creates {b} at {c} and switches to it.
w.stash: Puts your uncommitted changes aside so the working folder is clean.
w.pop: Brings back "{m}" and removes it from the stash list.
w.undo: Each risky step saved an undo point. Restoring puts every branch back where it was then.
w.merge: Adds the {n} commits of {a} into {b} with a merge commit. History is kept as it was.
w.rebase: Replays the {n} commits of {a} on top of {b}, so the history is a straight line. The commits get new ids.
w.interactive: Edit the commits of {b} since {base}: drag to reorder, then keep, reword, squash into the one above, or drop.
w.cherry: Copies "{c}" onto {b} as a new commit.
w.revert: Adds a new commit that undoes "{c}". History is kept.
w.resetsoft: Moves {b} back to "{c}". The later changes stay, staged.
w.resetmixed: Moves {b} back to "{c}". The later changes stay in the folder, unstaged.
w.resethard: Moves {b} back to "{c}" and throws away the later changes in the folder.
w.pr: Opens a draft pull request from {a} into {b}, with the task report as its text.
w.delete: Deletes {b} here and on the remote.

nb.taskHint: Fills in the name below. Leave it and type a name yourself if you prefer.
nb.name: Branch name
nb.bad: git does not allow this name (.., ~ ^ : ? * [ \, //, a trailing / or .lock).
nb.exists: A branch with this name already exists.

adv.title: Advice ({n})
adv.sub: From fixed rules on the repository: no AI, 0 tokens
adv.none: Nothing to do: every branch is up to date, pushed and tidy.
adv.ruleHint: The rule that produced this advice (docs/plans/git-sync.md §14)
adv.openPRNote: Opens PR #{n} and its CI log in the browser.
adv.onBaseWhy: Work on the base branch skips review and the board. Move it to a branch, then open a PR.
adv.mergedWhy: Every commit of this branch is in main. Deleting it keeps the list short; an undo point is saved first.
adv.ciFailWhy: The PR cannot be merged until the checks pass. Read the CI log, fix, and push again.
adv.behindClean: No file is touched on both sides, so no conflict is expected. {reason}
adv.behindClash: Expect a conflict in {files}: both sides changed it. Doing it now, while it is small, is easier. {reason}

reason.local: The branch is only on this machine, so rebasing rewrites nothing anyone else has.
reason.pushedSolo: It is pushed but only you use it: rebasing needs a force-push (with lease), which a person approves.
reason.shared: Others see it (open PR or someone else's branch): merging keeps its history instead of rewriting it.

adv.wipWhy: Commits like {msgs} make the history hard to read. Squash or reword them before review.
adv.behindRemote: {b} is {n} commit(s) behind its remote copy
adv.behindRemoteWhy: Someone pushed to this branch. Pull before you add more, or your push will be refused.
adv.divergedWhy: It has also {ahead} commit(s) of yours that the remote does not: pull (merge) first, then push.
adv.aheadWhy: Push so the team (and CI) can see them. A person approves the push.
adv.notPushed: {b} exists only on this machine ({n} commit(s))
adv.notPushedWhy: If this machine is lost, so is the work. Push it, then open a draft PR when it is ready to show.
adv.bigWhy: Over {max} lines is hard to review well. Consider a new branch for the next part.
adv.staleWhy: Is it still needed? Finish it, hand it over, or delete it so its claim stops blocking others.
adv.overlapWhy: Both touch {files}. Agree who goes first; the second one rebases after the first is merged.
adv.oldStashWhy: "{m}": bring it back or drop it, so it is not lost or forgotten.

live.reverted: Commit undone with a new commit.
live.notRepo: This project folder is not a git repository.
live.allResolved: Every file is resolved. Continue to finish.

mcp.title: MCP connections
mcp.lede: Give the agent tools from other programs (Blender, Roblox Studio, game engines) and web services. Hermes keeps the setting; new chats get the tools.
mcp.placeLocal: This machine: web MCPs and local programs
mcp.allowLocal: Local programs: allowed on your own machine
mcp.noLocal: Local programs: not on a server. Connect them in hpk on your own machine.
mcp.blockLocal: A local program runs only on a person's own machine. Connect it in hpk on your computer.
mcp.blockLoop: This URL is an app on a person's machine. Connect it in hpk on your computer.
mcp.connectedSub: Green: on. Grey: saved but off (test it to switch on). Red: not allowed here. New chats get the tools; open chats need /reload-mcp.
mcp.none: No MCP yet. Pick one below.

state.off: Saved, off: test it when the program is open

mcp.testTip: Connect now and list its tools
mcp.removeConfirm: Remove MCP "{name}"? The agent loses its tools in new chats.
mcp.addSub: Ready-made settings; every field can be changed before connecting.
mcp.addSubServer: Server: web MCPs only. Locked cards connect from hpk on your own machine.
mcp.have: Already added: open it to change
mcp.savedOff: Saved, but switched off: it did not answer
mcp.reloadNote: Open chats keep their tools; type /reload-mcp in a chat or start a new one.
mcp.viewOnly: Only an owner can add or remove MCPs.

f.name: Name
f.nameHint: Short, a-z 0-9 - _. Tools appear as mcp__<name>__<tool>.
f.nameBad: Use a short name: a-z, 0-9, - and _
f.commandHint: The command Hermes starts, or the full path to it.
f.argsHint: Separated by spaces; quote one that has spaces.
f.tokenHint: Optional. Goes to Hermes (its .env), never to hpk or the page.
f.tokenWin: On Windows Hermes reads tokens from the keyboard: add this one in a terminal with hermes mcp add.

need.local: Runs on this machine. Install the program first; Hermes starts it when a chat needs it.
need.blender: Needs uv (for uvx) and the Blender add-on from the guide, enabled in Blender, with Blender open.
need.roblox: Needs Roblox's Studio MCP server installed (see the guide) and Studio open with its plugin. Use the full path to rbx-studio-mcp if it is not on PATH.
need.godot: Needs Node.js (npx). Set GODOT_PATH to your Godot program.
need.figma: Needs the Figma desktop app with its local MCP server switched on. Only on your own machine.
need.playwright: Needs Node.js (npx). Opens a browser the agent can drive.
need.files: Needs Node.js (npx). Replace <folder> with the one folder the agent may use.
need.context7: Up-to-date library docs. No key needed for light use.
need.deepwiki: Answers questions about public GitHub repositories. No key needed.
need.github: Needs a GitHub token. Remember: pushing and merging are red lines in hpk.

u.never: Not used yet. Counting starts with the first call in a chat.
u.noProjects: No project has used it yet.
u.noTools: No tool has been called yet.
u.noChats: No chat has used it yet.
u.sparkTip: {n} calls in all; bars: last 14 days

bg.title: Background jobs
bg.sub: What runs for the agent right now: commands Hermes started in the background and local MCP programs. Refreshes every 5 s.
bg.stopTip: Stop pid {pid} and what it started
bg.confirm: Stop "{what}" (pid {pid}) and what it started? Unsaved work in it is lost.
bg.sandbox: Runs in Hermes' sandbox: stop it from its chat

media.remote: On another website: the Console only shows files from the project
media.outside: Outside the project folder: not shown
media.cannotPlay: This browser cannot play this video format.
media.cannotLoad: The file could not be loaded.
media.label: Label
media.tooBig: Larger than 5 MB: open it in a new tab instead.
media.compressed: this glTF uses compressed meshes or textures (Draco, Meshopt or Basis), which need a decoder the Console does not load. Export without compression.
media.resume: Paused to save memory: click to show again
media.qDefaultTip: Use this quality for every new 3D view. It starts at Low.

browser.title: Browser
browser.lede: The AI's built-in browser on this machine. Watch every step live; take over any time. Recordings stay private to you.
browser.dockTip: Show the AI's browser beside the page
browser.dockSwap: Dock on the right / along the top
browser.idle: The browser is closed. It opens when the AI starts browsing, or start it yourself.
browser.needServe: The built-in browser runs in hpk serve on your own machine. Open the Console from hpk serve to use it.
browser.screenAria: Live view of the browser. When you drive, clicks, scrolling and keys go to the page.
browser.autoOpen: Open the browser panel when the AI starts browsing
browser.runsSub: Every browsing session: steps with a screenshot after each. Private to you, kept 30 days unless pinned, never put into the wiki.
browser.deleteConfirm: Delete this recording and its screenshots?
browser.privateNote: Private to you. Fields hpk filled from the vault are masked; values are never stored.

vault.title: Vault
vault.lede: Passwords, logins, tokens and .env values for the AI to use without ever seeing them. Kept on this machine only.
vault.deleteConfirm: Delete {{secret:{name}}}? The AI can no longer use it.
vault.revealConfirm: Show the value of {name} on this screen for 20 seconds?
vault.noSitesTip: The AI cannot use it until you add the sites it may be filled on.
vault.none: No secrets yet. Add one; the AI will only see its name.
vault.listSub: Click one to change it. The AI sees only {{secret:name}} and the sites.
vault.shortWarn: Values shorter than 4 characters cannot be hidden from page text.
vault.aiNever: The AI never sees the value. hpk types it into the page itself, only on the sites listed here, and hides it from everything the AI reads and from recordings.

f.name: Name
f.nameHint: The AI writes {{secret:name}}; a login's user name is {{secret:name.user}}.
f.sitesHint: Comma separated. example.com is that site only; write *.example.com to include its subdomains. https only.

vault.envSub: hpk writes the values into the project's .env; the AI is blocked from reading those files.
vault.mcpTitle: Give the AI the built-in browser
vault.mcpBody: Adds the hpk-browser MCP to Hermes (on this machine). New chats get open, click, type, fill_secret and screenshot.

keeper.dpapiTip: Encrypted with a key only your Windows account can open (DPAPI).
keeper.keychainTip: The key is in your macOS Keychain.
keeper.secret-serviceTip: The key is in your desktop keyring.
keeper.fileTip: No OS keyring here: the key is a file only your account can read. Weaker than an OS keyring.

vault.how4s: the name again, never the value

pin.setBody: Changing, deleting or showing a secret needs this PIN. Type it only here: the AI never sees it, so programs it runs cannot unlock the vault.
pin.unlockBody: Unlocked for 10 minutes on this screen.
pin.pin: PIN (8 or more characters; 10+ if digits only)
pin.unlockTip: Locked: changes, deletes and showing values need your PIN

ts.title: Team server
ts.lede: Join your team's hpk server from this machine. Work stays here; the team's board, wiki, approvals and people come from the server.
ts.notHere: This page is for hpk on a person's own machine. A team server does not join another server.
ts.joinSub: An owner gives you the address and a one-time code
ts.urlHint: Starts with https://. hpk checks the certificate as usual.
ts.codeHint: Ten letters and digits, one use, expires 15 minutes after it was made.
ts.deviceHint: Shown in the device list, so you know which one to revoke. Empty = the computer name.
ts.safeBody: The server gives this machine its own device token. hpk keeps it in your vault, hidden: it is not in the vault list, the AI cannot name it or read it, and it never goes into a page or a log. The server keeps only its SHA-256.
ts.ownerBody: An owner makes one on the server, or from their own hpk on this page once they joined:
ts.revokedHelp: The server no longer accepts this device. Leave, then join again with a new code from an owner.
ts.leaveConfirm: Leave {url}? This device is revoked on the server and its token removed from this machine.
ts.pinAsk: Vault PIN (removing the device token needs it):
ts.myDevicesSub: Every machine you joined from. Revoke one you lost or no longer use.
ts.noWork: The server sent no board for you (your projects may be limited).
ts.noClaims: Nobody holds a claim right now.
ts.revokeConfirm: Revoke {name}? That device stops working at once and needs a new code to join again.
ts.inviteSub: For someone already in the team
ts.inviteHint: A one-time code (15 minutes) to join from their own hpk.
ts.codeOnce: One use. Works until {time}. Send it privately, with the server address.
ts.ownerOnServer: Invite codes, people, roles and revoking someone else's device are done in the team server's own Console. Your hpk here never makes credentials: any program on this machine, the AI included, can call it.

pwa.label: App
pwa.why: Opens HPK Console in its own window, from the Start menu, Dock or app list. It is the same web app: nothing native is added.
pwa.done: Installed. Open HPK Console from your apps.
pwa.later: Not installed. You can do it later here.

hint.chrome: To install: the install icon at the right of the address bar, or ⋮ → Cast, save and share → Install page as app.
hint.edge: To install: ⋯ → Apps → Install this site as an app.
hint.safari: To install: File → Add to Dock (Safari 17 or newer).
hint.ios: To install: Share → Add to Home Screen.
hint.firefox: Firefox does not install web apps on the desktop. Keep it in a pinned tab, or open the Console in Chrome or Edge to install it.
hint.other: If your browser can install web apps, look for "Install" or "Add to home screen" in its menu.

login.label: Start hpk when I log in
login.hint: Runs hpk serve in the background after you log in, for you only. No window opens.

how.windows: Windows: a Task Scheduler task named "hpk" for your account (no administrator rights).

login.unsupported: Start at login is not available on {os}.
login.unavailable: Start at login can be set only in hpk on your own machine.
login.on: hpk will start when you log in
login.off: hpk will no longer start at login

desk.title: Desktop notices on this computer
desk.hint: Through your browser, on any OS. The browser asks once for permission.
desk.blocked: Notices are blocked for this site in the browser. Allow them in the site settings (the icon left of the address), then turn this on.
desk.unsupported: This browser cannot show desktop notices here (it needs notification support and a secure page: 127.0.0.1 or HTTPS).
desk.denied: The browser did not allow notices.
desk.away: Only when the Console is in the background
desk.testBody: Desktop notices work on this computer.
desk.approval: The agent is waiting for you
desk.browserDriver: The agent wants the browser back. Hand it back in the Console.
desk.browserVault: The agent needs the vault unlocked.

key.title: This browser can look but not change anything
key.body: Changes need the Console opened from hpk. In a terminal run
